clue.text: Glamour industry model whose sins include bush, but no tail

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters that follow are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: no tail says the last letter of the word bush is dropped

explanation.surface: A sniping remark about a glamour model's private life, with a schoolboy double meaning for good measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun naming the woman but it is the anagram signal; 'no tail' trims BUSH to BUS, and 'include' just adds those letters to WHOSE SINS before the whole lot is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment, film and television are together known as the world of glitz and glamour.

clue.text: After forgetting English, Swiss girl adopts new language

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one letter is taken inside the shortened name
after forgetting says a letter is first lost from the girl's name

parts.note: Heidi is the Swiss girl of Johanna Spyri's children's novel

explanation.surface: A Swiss girl loses her English and picks up a new language.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIDI less E gives HIDI; N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the principal official tongue of India.

clue.text: I drink bottles — he might benefit from higher 7 21

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold in, so the drink word encloses the letter I

parts.note: water is something to drink

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a drinking problem, then grumbles about who profits from a bigger restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 21 is SERVICE CHARGE, the two answers read together; the restaurant tip it adds goes to the staff who serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant staff who serve tables usually get a share of the service charge, so a higher one helps them.

clue.text: Is loan arranged with credit union initially bad for company?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word union
arranged says the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: C is short for credit

explanation.surface: A worried question about a loan set up with a credit union damaging a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' looks like a firm, as the loan story suggests, but it means other people's society. The union's opening letter leads; 'arranged' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shy of social life, poor at mixing with others, is described as being bad company.

clue.text: One, ten and a hundred divide precisely into three or so

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to divide is to split, so the numerals for ten and a hundred cut the adverb open
into three says the adverb ends up in three pieces, the numerals falling either side of its middle vowel

parts.note: neatly means precisely, tidily
X is the Roman numeral ten
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle: one, ten and a hundred dividing exactly into three, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divide ... into three' looks like sums; the Roman ten and hundred split the word for precisely into three parts, landing either side of its A, with the Roman one in front.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Or so' means approximately, without exact accuracy.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide, is called this
over as in left over: additional, more than needed

explanation.surface: Run over
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs scored without the batter hitting the ball, such as byes and wides.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye run is listed among the cricket sundries, and anything surplus is additional.

clue.text: Priest's work: lecture on sin, Monday off sinning

indicators.note: off says the day's abbreviation is removed from the lecture

parts.note: a sermon is a moral lecture, often on sin
vice is wrongdoing, sinning

explanation.surface: A priest's routine: preaching about sin, taking Monday off to indulge in some.
explanation.walkthrough: SERMON less MON leaves SER, then VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A church service, the worship led by a priest, is a central part of his job.

clue.text: About a third of customers missed 7 21

indicators.note: about means around, so the tennis word goes round the letters taken from customers

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve the receiver fails to touch: a missed service

indicators.note: a third of picks the opening three of the nine letters of customers

explanation.surface: A complaint that a third of diners went without the service charge, or skipped it.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is SERVICE and 21 CHARGE: a missed service in tennis is an ace, which 'About' wraps round the opening third of customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a charge against someone is to formally blame them for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Caesar's foot pokes through new special hole in abdomen

indicators.note: to poke through something is to get into it, so one letter is put inside the rearranged word
new says the letters of special are made into a new arrangement
the foot of a word is its end, so this picks the final letter of Caesar

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor's foot poking through a specially made hole in someone's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' wants to be Latin PES; it is just the last letter of Caesar, R, placed inside the anagram of SPECIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects breathe through small openings along the sides of their bodies, called breathing pores.

clue.text: Protection against kids worn by a big chicken

parts.note: a cap is a contraceptive diaphragm, protection against having children
something worn is on

explanation.surface: A risqué image of contraception worn by a cowardly giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' suggests a coward, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table grows large.

clue.text: Rank noises made by pub ghost

indicators.note: noises made says the clue wants a word that sounds like the phrase that follows

parts.note: a pub is an inn and a ghost a spectre

explanation.surface: A haunted pub where the ghost makes horrible noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul, describing the noises, but it is a police rank. INN SPECTRE said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British police forces a detective's grade above sergeant is one of the ranks.

clue.text: Downfall for Scots among others, wanting European state

indicators.note: wanting means needing, so the downpour word needs the letter for European after it

parts.note: the Scots are one of the peoples of the United Kingdom, abbreviated UK
rain is what falls down from the sky

explanation.surface: Bad weather for the Scots and other Britons, who are apparently missing Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' looks like ruin; it is rainfall, the weather the UK gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a sovereign country of eastern Europe, a nation.

clue.text: Tea bags butter bread

indicators.note: to bag is to capture and hold, so the tea word holds the butter word

parts.note: chai is a name for tea
a pat is a small slab of butter

explanation.surface: A shopping list or recipe: tea bags, butter, bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea bags' looks like an item; 'bags' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from Indian cookery.

clue.text: Herewith, a poem to make nonsense of

parts.note: enc. (enclosed) is written on a letter to mean herewith
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Someone submits a poem with a covering note, inviting it to be ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make nonsense of' suggests mockery, but it means turning a message into apparent gibberish.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a message into cipher turns it into gibberish for anyone without the key.

clue.text: 7 21 racket arranged with Tyneside restaurateurs at its heart

indicators.note: with ... at its heart says the other letters sit in the middle of the racket-and-arranged pair

parts.note: a din is a loud racket
set means arranged, put in place
NE is the north-east of England, where Tyneside lies

indicators.note: at its heart picks the central letter of the thirteen in restaurateurs

explanation.surface: Complaint about restaurants running a service charge racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is SERVICE in the crockery sense; 21 (CHARGE) only colours the surface. 'at its heart' does double duty: the north-east plus the heart of restaurateurs go in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A matched set of plates and dishes for a meal is a service, as in a dinner service.

clue.text: 7 21 at Dido's place

indicators.note: service, the answer at 7, means overhaul or repair, so the letters that follow are reworked

parts.note: the answer at 21 is charge

explanation.surface: A service charge levied at the queen of Carthage's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 21 reads as SERVICE CHARGE, but here 'service' is the anagram signal working on CHARGE and AT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid Dido is the queen and founder of the North African city.

clue.text: Cold rock concert finally brought inside by shivering roadies

indicators.note: says one letter is put within the rearranged letters
shivering suggests shaking, so the letters of roadies are shaken into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word concert

explanation.surface: Roadies shiver after a cold rock concert, the gear finally brought inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold rock' looks like music in a chilly venue; it is a lump of rock in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor planets are icy or stony bodies circling the sun: rocks in the cold of space.

clue.text: Cast off clothing

parts.note: reads as second-hand clothes thrown away; casting off is how knitters finish a piece

explanation.surface: Cast off clothing
explanation.walkthrough: Casting off is the final step in making a knitted garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers and cardigans are finished by casting off stitches from the needles.

clue.text: Successfully 7d 21d

parts.note: read as serviced and charged successfully: an animal served by a male, or a thing full and loaded

explanation.surface: Successfully 7d 21d
explanation.walkthrough: To service a female animal is to mate with her; to be charged is to be loaded, and a word is called pregnant with meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A successful mating leaves a female animal carrying young, laden or full.

clue.text: Erecting a little cupola sure provides a view

indicators.note: Erecting says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Putting up a small domed roof certainly gives you a good outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, erecting means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful look over something, a reading, is a perusal, as in taking a view of a document.

clue.text: Arcane criticism of setter is a little excessive

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so his own is my

indicators.note: says the word for criticism has a little too much: one letter more than wanted, which comes off

parts.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them

explanation.surface: The setter complains that the criticism he gets is rather over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: MY STICK is one letter too long, so lose the end K.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mystic is spiritually obscure, beyond ordinary understanding, like secret lore.

clue.text: Case of gangrene found by lady who cleans ward

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaning lady

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so this picks its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cleaner on a hospital ward discovers a case of gangrene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ward' looks like a hospital ward; it is a person in someone's care. CHAR, a British term for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A child or person placed in someone's care is their responsibility, their ward.

clue.text: Upset girls hiding at German camp full of belligerent men

definitions.text: German camp full of belligerent men

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards
hiding says one word is concealed within the other

parts.note: gals is a casual word for girls

explanation.surface: Distressed girls hide in a German camp full of aggressive men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns the whole thing upside down, which in a down entry means reading it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime German prison camps held captured soldiers, enemy servicemen from the fighting.

clue.text: Most dodgy half-time snacks full of rubbish? On the contrary

indicators.note: full of says one word holds another
says the containment is the other way round: the rubbish holds the snacks, not the reverse

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense
pies are the classic food eaten at football matches at half-time

explanation.surface: Questioning whether the half-time pies are packed with junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the rubbish fills the snacks; 'On the contrary' swaps that, so the snacks go inside the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British for poor quality or dubious, so the superlative means of the worst quality.

clue.text: Hit film the kids saw with mum smuggled inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is put within the film rating

parts.words: film the kids saw with mum
parts.note: a PG film is Parental Guidance, one children may watch with a parent
to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running

explanation.surface: A hit film that children watched with their mum, sneaked into the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To prang a car is to crash it, so it means to strike or collide with.

clue.text: Greek establishment's near broke after tax is misdirected

indicators.note: after says the broken word follows the tax letters
misdirected says the tax letters are sent the wrong way, rearranged

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: broke means smashed, so the letters of near are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A Greek business is nearly bankrupt after a tax bill went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT becomes TAV and NEAR becomes ERNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant or café.

clue.text: What Tories did for Thatcher's victory over Heath?

definitions.text: What Tories did for Thatcher's victory over Heath?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
Ted Heath, Conservative prime minister whom Margaret Thatcher beat for the party leadership in 1975

explanation.surface: A political-history question about the 1975 Conservative leadership contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath is Edward 'Ted' Heath, British prime minister 1970-74, deposed as party leader by Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative MPs cast ballots for Thatcher, making her their leader in 1975.

clue.text: Terrible suffering of hero that shed light on the Somme?

definitions.text: that shed light on the Somme?

parts.note: a hero is a star, and 'of' gives the possessive S
hell is terrible suffering

explanation.surface: A hero's dreadful ordeal in the First World War trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme was a 1916 First World War battle, as the surface's war hero suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell bursting in the air to light up enemy positions was used at night in the trenches.

clue.text: Good to put an end to slight obsession

indicators.note: says the letter is placed at the end of the slender word

parts.note: thin means slight, slender

explanation.surface: A recommendation to stop a minor fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put an end to' sounds like stopping something; it means placing G at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to have a fixation or preoccupation with it.

clue.text: A disastrous blunder, telling these men in 7 21!

definitions.text: A disastrous blunder, telling these men in 7 21!

parts.words: A disastrous blunder, telling these men in 7 21!
parts.note: points to a famous misunderstood order of 1854 that sent cavalry on a doomed charge

explanation.surface: A disastrous blunder, telling these men in 7 21!
explanation.walkthrough: 7 21 here is the cavalry charge at Balaclava in the Crimean War, made famous by Tennyson's poem 'Someone had blundered'.
explanation.definitionFit: British light cavalry made the doomed Balaclava charge after an ambiguous order.
